compiler: deterministic regex parse (engine/policy_compiler.py); no LLM call
rule_text: Disputed but legitimate. When the customer disputes a charge that matches their own recurring pattern (same merchant, same amount, monthly), recommend `CREATE_CASE`, `VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER`, and `WARN_CUSTOMER`. Do not block.

parse.note: applies to a dispute, i.e. a customer_report case
the data has no merchant id; the engine's recurring check uses the same proxy
monthly read as a median gap of 25-35 days

parse.why_not_in_text: 'pattern' gives no count; two prior gaps make a pattern

sql_template: WITH target AS ( SELECT t.id, t.TransactionID, t.card_id, t.customer_id, t.ts, t.amt, t.product_cd, CASE WHEN t.channel = 'in_person' THEN t.addr1 ELSE t.p_email END AS merchant FROM txc t WHERE t.id IN ({target_ids}) ), prior AS ( SELECT g.id AS target_id, p.ts FROM target g JOIN txc p ON p.card_id = g.card_id AND p.product_cd = g.product_cd AND p.ts < g.ts AND p.ts <= '{as_of}' AND abs(p.amt - g.amt) <= {amount_tol} * g.amt AND (CASE WHEN p.channel = 'in_person' THEN p.addr1 ELSE p.p_email END) = g.merchant AND g.merchant <> '' ), gaps AS ( SELECT target_id, date_diff('second', lag(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY target_id ORDER BY ts), ts) / 86400.0 AS gap_d FROM (SELECT target_id, ts FROM prior UNION ALL SELECT id, ts FROM target) ) SELECT g.id, g.card_id, g.customer_id, g.ts::VARCHAR, g.amt, g.merchant, count(x.gap_d) AS n_prior, median(x.gap_d) AS median_gap_days FROM target g JOIN gaps x ON x.target_id = g.id GROUP BY ALL HAVING count(x.gap_d) >= {min_prior} AND median(x.gap_d) BETWEEN {gap_min_d} AND {gap_max_d} ORDER BY g.id
